transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm... well, I'm on leave from work right now. I guess things got out of hand with a project. I pushed ahead with this new onboarding launch, and... I committed company money and vendor time before I actually had the approvals in place. At the time, I just... I felt like it was bold, like it was what needed to be done. But now... yeah. Now everyone is asking what I was thinking, and I'm here.
During the time you were working on this project, did you feel unusually high, elated, or irritable — like you had more energy or needed less sleep?

I don't know about "high." I just... for the past few weeks, I felt really alive. Like I could finally show leadership what HR can actually be. 

But... yeah, I guess I was irritable, too. If someone questioned me... even over really small edits, or just routine budget questions... I would get suddenly furious. I just... didn't have the patience for it.
Did you find yourself needing less sleep than usual during this time?
I... I guess so. I didn't really think about it much. I just woke up early and started working.
How many hours of sleep did you typically get during this time?
I don't know exactly. Maybe... three or four hours? I just didn't feel tired.
During this time, did you find yourself doing a lot more activities than usual — like starting new projects, working longer hours, or being constantly on the move?

I suppose. I mean... I kept getting to the office early. Sitting at my desk just felt... almost impossible. Like my body had a motor in it or something. 

So I was just constantly moving. Walking the floors... rewriting decks, emailing people... rearranging our plans. I just... kept going.
During this time, did you feel unusually good about yourself — like you were on top of the world, or had special abilities or insights that others didn't?
No... I don't think so. I just felt like I had a lot to do. I didn't think I was special or anything. Just... busy.

Can you think back to that time — was there a period where your mood was clearly different than usual, lasting at least several days? Like feeling unusually upbeat, overly confident, or easily agitated in a way that was not typical for you?

I guess... yes, it was different. For the past few weeks, I just felt... I don't know, really alive. Like I finally had the energy to show the leadership team what our department could actually do. But then... if someone questioned me, even just about a small edit on a slide or a routine budget thing, I would get so angry. Just... furious, really fast. It wasn't like me.
Was there a specific time during this period where your mood was consistently different — like feeling unusually upbeat, energized, or irritable — every day for at least four days in a row?

Four days? I mean... it's been longer than that. It's... it's been building for about a month, I suppose. Right around the time the... the new executive started. They started challenging my onboarding redesign, and... yeah. It's been going on since then.

Can you think back to that time—was there a stretch of at least four days in a row where your mood was clearly different than usual, like feeling unusually upbeat, overly energized, or easily agitated every day?
I... I thought I just said that. Yes. It's been about a month, so... definitely more than four days in a row. It was just every day. I don't really know what else to add.
After this period of feeling very energetic and irritable, did you experience a time where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
Not really, no. I... I don't think I've felt hopeless or anything. I just haven't noticed feeling like that.
During that time when you felt so energetic and irritable, was there also a period where you actually felt unusually happy or elevated—like on top of the world—for several days in a row?

I don't know if I'd say "happy," exactly. Just... alive. Like I could finally show the leadership team what HR is supposed to be. But then... well, I'd get furious if someone questioned me. Even over just small edits to a document, or routine budget questions. It's just been a mix of that for the past few weeks.
Was there a time during this period when your mood was not just irritable but actually elevated—like feeling unusually confident, excited, or on top of the world—for several days in a row?

I thought I just answered that... I don't know about "excited." Like I said, for the past few weeks it's just been either feeling brilliantly alive, where I can finally show leadership what HR can be... or suddenly getting furious if someone questions me over small edits or routine budgets. I don't really have another way to describe it.
Was there a time when your mood was not just irritable but actually elevated — like feeling unusually confident, excited, or on top of the world — for several days in a row?
I... I feel like we're going in circles here. I just told you. It's been the same for the last few weeks. Just... what I already said. I don't know what else you want me to say about it.

Can you think back and tell me if there was a time when, instead of just feeling irritable, you actually felt unusually confident, powerful, or like you were on top of the world for several days in a row?

I really don't know how many different ways I can answer this. I've been telling you... it's just been the same for the past few weeks. Either I feel brilliantly alive, like I finally have the power to show the leadership team what HR is actually supposed to be... or I get furious if they question me over some small edit or a routine budget thing. That's... that's just what it is.

Can you think back and tell me if there was a time when, instead of just feeling irritable, you actually felt unusually confident, powerful, or like you were on top of the world for at least four days in a row?

I... look, we've been over this. It's been the same for weeks. I feel... brilliant, like I can finally fix things at work, show them what my department can actually do. And then... I just get so angry if they push back on stupid things, like budget lines. It's just been that. For weeks. I don't know what else to tell you.

Can you think back and tell me if there was a time when your mood was not just irritable but actually elevated — like feeling unusually confident, excited, or on top of the world — for at least four days in a row?

I... I feel like I'm repeating myself. I just... I don't know what else to say. It's been the same for weeks. I feel like I can finally fix things, like I'm brilliantly alive and can show them what my department can actually do. But then... I just get so angry if they push back on stupid things, like budget lines or small edits. It's just been that. For weeks.

Can you think back and tell me if there was a time when your mood was not just irritable but actually elevated — like feeling unusually confident, excited, or on top of the world — for at least four days in a row?

Look... I really don't have a different answer for you. Yes. For the last few weeks. It's just... feeling brilliant, like I can finally show leadership what we can actually do... or getting completely furious over a routine budget question. That's... that's all I can tell you.
